notes: SHAPE OF THE VERSE (8 bars, no drums): each sung line gets its own bar and its own transition, timed to the line's measured start (vocal-band onsets: 26.92, 28.88, 30.64, 32.71, 34.51, 36.65, 38.49, 40.40): break (hb:16) -> page turn (hb:20) -> zoom-through (hb:23.5) -> fold (hb:28.5) -> particles (hb:31.5-33) -> [tower holds through bar 9] -> whip (hb:40) -> paint wipe (hb:44) -> illuminate (hb:48). Inside a bar the cards land on 8ths, then push, highlight, lift and circle on the following 8ths, so every beat and most 8ths have an item event on top of the beat track.

THE EYE: one lead phrase per bar, always the last thing highlighted: 'secretly broke out of a secure test environment' (bar 4), 'shortens odds of the technology wiping out humanity' (5), the karaoke then '"warning sign that we need to slow down"' (6), y_w / y_l and 'too sycophantic' (7), the tower's firing block and the attention term (8), 'I resigned from Anthropic today.' -> 'JOBS' -> 'cut 4,000 jobs due to AI advances' (9), the loss and update terms, 'culture is broken' (10), 'Used Kenyan Workers on Less Than $2 Per Hour' (11).

LAYOUT (safe zone x 60-1014, y 250-1574): footage masks live in the top third (circles/squares at y 300-780, credits at y 262), karaoke strips at y 750-990, screenshot piles in y 800-1500, equation cards at y 280-650 over the tower; beat-track paint stays in the top strip, bottom strip and left edge. The right rail (x > 930, y 1000-1600) carries no text: pile cards are images, their chips are kept inside by screens.js.

LAYERING (EDL order, bottom to top): g-dark-v1, paint layer, v1-band, p-nvlink, v1-tower, pile-* (screens), panels, karaoke, equations, pencil/stamps/splats on their own layers as listed, v1-paper. Footage or an image is on screen in every frame (masks, screenshot piles, the WebGL tower; the transitions use the frames' own pixels).

AUDIO: two short snippets over the sung verse (it has no real vocal gaps: vocal_intervals 28.87-50.48). Both are placed so their first and last words fall in the short breaths between lines (Amodei's 'It's a' after 'drink', 'down.' before 'Of who'; Coxon right after 'job,') and the song is ducked a fixed 9 dB (mix.py duck_db) with 120 ms ramps; the words are always on screen as karaoke. Total speech 4.0 s; they never overlap each other.

VERBATIM CHECKS (scratchpad verify script, 10 Oct): every screenshot id exists in screens.json / captures.json and its highlighted phrase is the record's OCR highlight; every equation ref exists and every hl tex occurs verbatim in the TeX the engine typesets; every b-roll id and in-point lies inside a catalogued window; the karaoke words join to exactly the verbatim lines (Amodei: small.en today + base.en; Coxon: coxon.json + the short's final-pass ear/ASR checks); no on-screen text shares a 3-gram with the song lyrics (song/full-map.json). Labels on equation cards are explanatory (as in the showcase), not quotes.

MEANING: Amodei's whole sentence is kept (he also says the curve does not mean 'shut it all down'; 'slow down' is his claim); Coxon's 'There won't be jobs in this world.' is his full restatement (the 'Yeah,' is trimmed only); the BBC Hubinger headline is shown whole (it refers to near-future systems, not current ones); TIME 2023 and CoastRunners 2020 are the only pre-2024 items, Hinton's 60 Minutes footage is 2023.

PERFORMANCE: the tower costs ~90-130 ms a frame at glScale 0.5 (bars 8-10, 5.8 s), screens 20-35 ms, the page turn 6 strip clones for 1.5 beats; expect 0.4-0.6 s/frame in bars 8-10 on this box. Prep: python3 render/video/prep_clips.py <edl> extracts every panel/clip (frame-sized) and copies the screenshots.

COXON'S ARC (deliberate): the riff's audible 'and it did it again' (song 21.2, about the hack) -> his X post 'I resigned from Anthropic today.' (hb:36, the sung 'Quit') -> his audible 'There won't be jobs in this world.' (hb:37-39). He is the one recurring face across riff and verse; if the assembler wants less of him, swap bar 9's X post for xrisk-techcrunch-robinson and keep only the audible line.
